sample_unit: survey respondents with at least one telehealth visit in prior 12 months (HINTS 7)

links.outcome: Group fairness metrics (Disparate Impact, Equal Opportunity) across sex and race/ethnicity
links.effect: Group fairness metrics revealed disparities across sex and race/ethnicity; individual counterfactual flip rates were low (sex CFR 0.024; race/ethnicity CFR 0.013).
links.quote: Group fairness metrics revealed disparities across sex and race/ethnicity, whereas individual counterfactual analyses indicated low flip rates (sex CFR: 0.024; race/ethnicity CFR: 0.013).

links.outcome: Counterfactual flip rate when sex or race/ethnicity attribute is changed
links.effect: Low counterfactual flip rates: sex CFR 0.024; race/ethnicity CFR 0.013.
links.quote: Group fairness metrics revealed disparities across sex and race/ethnicity, whereas individual counterfactual analyses indicated low flip rates (sex CFR: 0.024; race/ethnicity CFR: 0.013).

unlisted_practices: Developing a parsimonious interpretable point score and comparing it with ML models using SHAP feature importance

screen.reason: Empirical study developing and evaluating machine learning models and a risk score to predict telehealth discontinuation using survey data, including algorithmic fairness evaluation across sex and race/ethnicity, but without testing a comparative deployment intervention.
